hints.title: Boundary Delta Formulation
hints.text: Reversing subarray nums[L..R] only alters two adjacent difference terms: |nums[L-1] - nums[R]| and |nums[L] - nums[R+1]|.

hints.title: Interval Overlap Algebra
hints.text: For interior reversals, the change equals 2 * max(0, min(pair_max) - max(pair_min)) across disjoint interval pairs.

hints.title: Prefix and Suffix Boundary Edge Cases
hints.text: Explicitly check boundary reversals where L=0 or R=N-1 to catch changes that only affect one interval interface.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxValueAfterReverse(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        base = sum(abs(nums[i] - nums[i + 1]) for i in range(len(nums) - 1))
        n = len(nums)
        res = base

        for i in range(n - 1):
            res = max(res, base - abs(nums[i] - nums[i + 1]) + abs(nums[0] - nums[i + 1]))
            res = max(res, base - abs(nums[i] - nums[i + 1]) + abs(nums[-1] - nums[i]))

        min_hi = float("inf")
        max_lo = float("-inf")
        for i in range(n - 1):
            a, b = nums[i], nums[i + 1]
            min_hi = min(min_hi, max(a, b))
            max_lo = max(max_lo, min(a, b))

        return max(res, base + max(0, (max_lo - min_hi) * 2))
```

complexity.notes: Single linear pass computes the interval extrema and prefix/suffix boundary maximums in O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all O(N^2) subarray reversal pairs causes Time Limit Exceeded on N=30,000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Interval algebra decomposes the quadratic pair comparison into decoupled minimums and maximums.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Interval overlap simplification and separate consideration of edge reversals.
